analysis:
Examined release-provider.yml head lines 559-1454 and release-swift.yml (path-filter additions plus metadata).

Changed behavior: a new step, 'Compute cluster runtime facts from the final signed app' (lines 1000-1025), runs after signing, notarization and final-bytes checks. It unsets r2_public_url and coordinator_url, deletes the signing keychain, and asserts the Developer ID identity is no longer listed (lines 1009-1016). It checks that the bundle hash is unchanged (line 1017), extracts the tar, and runs scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh on the extracted app. Facts are passed to 'prepare' only when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true, and in that mode a failure fails the job. Otherwise the step is continue-on-error and only warns.

Assessment against TB-009, T-034 and T-054: the signing identity is destroyed before any code from the built artifact executes, which is a good ordering. No secrets.* are referenced in the step or in the Show and Retain steps (1027-1070). The facts come from the CI-built, signed bytes whose hash is re-verified, so they add no new provider-controlled trust input. Facts are retained for 30 days and written to the step summary. They hold only model and cluster capability data, so I saw no sensitive exposure. The publication, staging and publish jobs (lines 1118-1394) look unchanged apart from passing --cluster-runtime.

Open questions I could not verify because the files were not supplied:
1. Whether scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh really runs the CLI with an empty environment, as the comments claim. Other job-level env, such as keychain password variables or GH tokens, is not visible here.
2. Whether the coordinator validates the new cluster_runtime block, which is platform-owned.

release-swift.yml only adds script paths to the push filters, which widens the staging-trigger scope slightly and does not weaken the prod tag gating.

No concrete regression was identified. needs_deeper_review is set because of the unseen facts script and the job-level env.
